safety_introduction_text:
Welcome, Future Engineer!
Today, you’ll be helping us operate a real machine that packs boxes!
You’ll follow the journey of a box through a high-tech line with motors, sensors, robots, and more.
But before we start moving anything...
Let’s learn how to stay safe! 🦺
buttoncontroller_safety:
This is your control panel
You have them on beginning and end of the installation. Top switches - to chose your controls ( BP1 - first control buttons, BP2 - second operation station)
Top switches for bottom and top - select your bottom and top parts (MTL - metal, PLSTC - plastic, BLCK - black part, WHT - white parts)
pRCS - press selection (P - pneumatics, H - hydraulics)
box_deposit_page:
This is your box deposit
You put boxes from the top of aluminium frame.
First, put bottom of the box, then top part
To activate system press Start button on button controller
emergency_button_page:
Emergency button
If during operation of the machine dangerous event occur, you need to press emergency button. It will stop system completely.
To resume, you need to unclick the button and press the start.
You have them on the beginning and the end of installation
emergency_button_page1: Note: same emergency buttons are used in real machines. If you see a dangerous situation on factory, always look for buttons that look like that to stop machine operation.
safety_door_page:
Emergency doors
In addition to the emergency buttons, you also have interlocked doors. If the door opens, particular zone on the machine stops. If the door is open, machine also won`t start.
Note: even with open doors, don`t put your fingers where you can see that it is dangerous or into the moving parts. Safety is always first!
safety_door_page1: Interesting: to know if the door is open or closed, system is using special switches. If they are open - stop the machine. You can see them on the bottom of the doors
safety_gear_page:
What workers wear to work?
Except buttons and doors, workers need to remember about their own safety. So everyone who works with machinery needs to wear special safety gear.
safety_gear_page1: Safety glasses: no small particles are getting into your eyes
safety_gear_page2: Special closes: protect against body scratches, high temperature and look fancy
safety_gear_page3: Gloves: protects you hands against scratches and injuries
safety_gear_page4: Safety shoes: if something heavy falls on your leg or you step on sharp part - they will protect you
conclusion_safety:
Now you are ready to go!
Machine is now in your complete operation. Just wanted to remind about some general rules:
introduction_leisure:
🎓 Welcome to Educational Mode!
You’re not just watching the machine —You’re learning how it works.
At each stop, we’ll pause the action and explain the cool tech behind it.
From motors and sensors to suction cups and robot arms —  you’ll explore what makes this machine come alive!
👉 Ready to discover how engineers build systems like this?  Let’s begin!
leisure_how_to_start: Pre load boxes in the box deposit and press start button on button control
welcome_pneumatics:
🌀 Push with Air: Welcome to Pneumatics!
This cylinder just pushed the box onto the conveyor belt. But how?
It’s powered by compressed air — that’s pneumatics!
💨 Air pressure fills the cylinder
→ piston moves
→ box gets pushed
Pneumatics are clean, fast, and great for jobs like this.
conveyor_leisure:
Conveyor in Action
Factories use conveyors to move boxes from one place to another — just like a moving sidewalk!
Belts roll, rollers spin, and boxes ride forward... hands-free!
Conveyors don’t move by magic — they’re powered by electric motors.
Motors spin the rollers underneath, pulling the belt along.
motor_leisure: But how does the motor work and where is it used? Watch a video to learn it
sensor_leisure:
Machines can’t see like humans — they use sensors to detect objects.
Sensors act like eyes, but they ‘see’ using light or sound!
rotator_page:
The box needs to turn before it can be placed. Let’s rotate it 90 degrees.
Machines don’t just move forward — they can rotate too! Component ina system that rotates is called a rotary actuator. It works like a muscle that turns things instead of pushing. Some use air (pneumatics), some use oil (hydraulics), and others use motors.
degrees_page:
The movement is measured in degrees — like turning a steering wheel!
If you take a circle and divide it into 360 equal pieces, you will get 360 degrees. So 30 degrees, is when you divide circle in 360 pieces first and then take 30 of them
pin_placing_page:
Next step: place pins into the box. They help parts lock together.
But we need to be very precise — the holes must line up just right!
degrees_quiz_page: So how many degrees our box in set up rotates? Choose one correct answer
conclusion_leisure:
You helped build and assemble a box using real factory tech!
Let’s review what you’ve used:
✔ Pneumatics
✔ Sensors
✔ Robotics
✔ Motors
✔ Hydraulic press
✔ Control logic
winner_award:
What Kind of Engineer Will You Be?
Choose your path:
Sensor Specialist
Robotic Arm Pro
Safety Leader
Automation Engineer
🎖 Award: Junior Engineer Badge!
hydraulics_page:
Hydraulics:
Uses oil
Slower, but more powerful
Used for heavy-duty pressing
magnetic_train_page:
Magnets inside the track create a controlled magnetic field.
The mover has metal coils that let it glide, stop, or speed up. This technology is also used in a modern Japaneese speed trains
presence_height_sensor:
This is a height sensor.
After presence sensor detected something, height sensor measures the height by elongating the part and touching the surface of the box
presence_sensor2:
This is a presence sensor.
But if something is blocking the sensor`s view and light beam returns faster, then sensor gives signal `Yes, there is something underneath`
presence_sensor1:
This is a presence sensor.
Sensor sends a light beam and when there is nothing underneath the sensor, beam return the same way
pneumatics_hydraulics_use1: In factories, machines choose between pneumatics (air) and hydraulics (oil) depending on the job. Let’s see where each one works best!
pneumatics_hydraulics_use2:
Pneumatics use compressed air.
They’re great for:
✔ Moving small parts
✔ Opening and closing doors
✔ Lifting light things
✔ Moving fast!
pneumatics_hydraulics_use3:
Hydraulics use pressurized oil.
They’re great for:
✔ Heavy presses
✔ Lifting cars (car jack!)
✔ Moving huge machines
✔ Holding high pressure safely
H_P_press1:
To press the top and bottom parts together, we have two options:
🔵 Pneumatics (air)
🔴 Hydraulics (oil)
H_P_press4:
But they look exactly the same!
How am I supposed to choose?
pneumatic_sucktion1:
Some machines don’t grab — they suck!
This is a pneumatic suction cup, and it just picked up the box!
sucktion_vacuum1:
The cup removes air and creates a vacuum — like magic air glue!
That’s how it holds things... using air pressure.
🧪 Try this: Take a cup at home, press it to your palm and suck air out — now it sticks!
Same effect when you are sucking drink from a strough - you create vacuum by inhaling air from the cup and it “picks up” the drink that is inside the cup
pick_and_place_automation1:
Now a robotic arm picks up the box and moves it to the next station.
This is called pick-and-place automation.
carthesian_introduction1:
Robots use coordinates — like a map with X, Y, and Z axes — to move with precision.
X, Y and Z called Cartesian coordinates. Imagine that movement up-down we will call Z movement, left-right movement - X movement, and front-back movement - Y movement. So if I say to the arm move -2 in X axis and 5 in Z axis means that arm moves 2 cm in left direction and 5 cm upwards. Interesting fact, arm always start moving from point (0, 0, 0) or X = 0, Y = 0, Z = 0. So start point is always with reference that arm didn`t move anywhere that`s why all coordinates are 0
communication_introduction1:
The box now moves from the first conveyor to the second.
Different machines are working together — passing parts like a team!
communication_introduction4: No, box is still not here
communication_introduction2_1:
Machines use signals to communicate.
One system says: ‘I’m done!’ → another replies: ‘Okay, I’m ready!’”
communication_introduction2_2:
I am done!
Placing the box on conveyor
communication_introduction2_4:
No, box is still not here,
He is still placing it.
When he is ready, I will tell you
communication_introduction3_1: So many things are going on! If components will be just shouting each other commands it is going to be difficult to hear each other. That`s why we have main brain of the machine - PLC. It is a control unit that handles communication between components. And also instead of worlds it uses programming languages like: IF sensor = triggered THEN start conveyor
communication_introduction3_2:
I am done!
Placing the box on conveyor
communication_introduction3_5:
There should be a box coming.
Do you see it?
rgb_1: RGB coloring is what helps sensor to understand colors. It was proven that all the colors can be made out of 3 main colors: Red, Green and Blue (that what letters RGB stands for). So to express colors in digital world we use a framework where we explain how much of each of these 3 colors are used: rgb(Red, Green, Blue), where 0 - is the lowest number and 255 - the biggest. So for example only red would be rgb(255, 0, 0) and white - rgb(255, 255, 255) - mix of all the colors. Would you be able to guess which colors are matching to what rgb color scheme?
pneumatic_sucktion_question1:
Not everything works with suction. What do you think this cup can pick up?
Click on the images to select. Multiple correct answers possible
pneumatic_sucktion_question2: Great! Suction needs a smooth, air-tight surface.
P_H_questions: Match the job with the right system! Select only the job where you would use hydraulic system
linear_actuator1:
This part of the machine slides the box bottom smoothly — but guess what? No wheels. No belts. No friction.
That’s a magnetic linear mover — like magic!
cathesian_quiz: Where would this coordinates would be placed? Click on the correct cells on the grid, check with numbers on the axis
cylinder_introduction:
We’re using compressed air to press the pins into the box.
Air goes into pneumatic cylinder and moves it forward. Just exactly like with suction, but here air goes in and not out.
cylinder_introduction_2: Let’s try different pressures. Pressure measures how much air is going into the system. In physics pressure is measured in Bars. Fun fact, your bicycle tires uses 2.5 Bars. What happens if we don’t get it right?
cylinder_introduction_2_5: Moves exactly how much it should move
cylinder_introduction_2_6: Breaks box, piston extends too much
